newsitem.title: USA: Union disappointed by Inland Steel contract.
newsitem.headline: Union disappointed by Inland Steel contract.

text.p: The United Steelworkers of America said Tuesday they are disappointed with a contract with Inland Steel Corp which was accepted by an arbitrator.

Earlier, Inland Steel Corp, a subsidiary of Inland Steel Industries, said its offer for 7,000 employees at its East Chicago plant was approved by an arbitrator. The contract runs through July 31, 1999.

It includes a $0.50 an hour raise retroactive to August 1 plus an additional $0.25 on August 1, 1997 and 1998. Improvements were also made in the employee pension plan and lump sums of $1,000 will be paid to employees in each of the three contract years.
"The union had proposed wage increases of $1.50 an hour rather than any lump sum payments," the union said in a statement. It said it also proposed different pension changes.
"(I)t had offered a persuasive argument for its position, and was disappointed by the outcome," the union said.
The union said the lump sum bonuses and pension increases will be addressed in bargaining in 1999.
